qt: to the Commission Sakis Arnaoutoglou (S&D) Subject:

Chalkidiki green olives – protected under a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) – are an important EU export product and a key source of income for producers and processors. At the same time, competition from non-EU table olives is increasing, while European producers have to comply with strict requirements on plant protection, the environment, safety, quality and traceability, bumping up production costs. Protecting a European PDO product entails more than just protecting its name; it also means ensuring a level playing field and coordinated action to strengthen its presence on international markets. With this in mind: 1.

Does the Commission intend to assess the impact of imports of table olives from nonEU countries on the competitiveness of European producers and the need for greater reciprocity in production and trade conditions?

Has the Commission examined whether these imports and the effects thereof warrant safeguard clauses or other trade defence measures, and has it received a request, communication or proposal from the Greek Government with a view to protecting the industry?
What specific tools does the Commission intend to use to protect, promote and increase the added value of the Chalkidiki green olive PDO, particularly in new international markets?
